the verbal mode was the most frequently used mode of communication in Second Life and that the nonverbal communication mode, which was the second most frequently used, played a key role in the proxemic organization of the students and in the verbal mode, in the organization of the task and in the management of the deictic references made by the students.
nonverbal communication plays a key role in the proxemic organization of students and the task they undertake.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: How can we better describe the communication modes in synthetic worlds and the relationships that exist between the verbal and non-verbal acts that are built in to the environment?
the study of the multimodal communication of language learners in a virtual world and the impact of nonverbal modes on the verbal mode.

how nonverbal communication can be integrated into the study of computer mediated communication in synthetic worlds and what its contribution to the understanding of the interaction between students is.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nonverbal communication is not autonomous but rather a support to verbal communication in Second Life.
nonverbal acts are not autonomous in Second Life but rather are closely linked to verbal acts and are used to secure the contextual information needed for verbal communication.
the use of non verbal communication in Second Life can be seen as an alternative to verbal communication, as an addition to it and as a way of supporting the verbal mode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a methodological framework to analyse multimodal communication in synthetic worlds and that the application of this method to a course in ARCHI21 has shown that nonverbal acts are not autonomous but are used to support verbal communication.
we can say that the nonverbal communication is a powerful means of communication in Second Life and can be considered as a means of communication in its own right.

nonverbal communication is a key element in the interaction between the students, and that the use of non-verbal communication in Second life is not only a means of communication in itself but also a means of securing verbal communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nonverbal communication modes in a synthetic world are not autonomous but rather are interwoven with verbal communication.

the use of a synthetic world such as Second Life can be an interesting and useful tool in the teaching of languages, especially in the case of CLIL courses where students are required to learn a new language in a new cultural context.
nonverbal communication is a key element in the organisation of students' interactions and the management of verbal communication in Second Life.
